body:
Codex (m3) did not claim this issue. A worker cannot reproduce the defect from the pushed code.

Facts, read at `upstream/main` `326c938b1`:

- The three tests are on `main`. `main` reads STEP files through the previous reader, and the issue says that the tests pass on the head of #2843 (`eae027d55`).
- The failure needs the importer switch (PR B of #917). No PR is open for it.
- The pushed branch `issue/917-solidcore-step` is at `776ba8b76` (`wip(import): read STEP through solidcore (held: fixtures refused)`). It is not stacked on #2843. It has no `known-fail #2849` marker.
- The last comments on #917 say that the PR B work is local, in the worktree `issue-917`.

Result: the pin cannot fail on `main`, and there is no open PR to stack on. A fix made now can also collide with the PR B work, which is in progress on the same tests.

This issue can be worked when PR B is pushed and its draft PR is open. Then a worker can stack on that PR. The maintainer decides if the issue gets `blocked` until then.

Diagnosis (branch `issue/917-solidcore-step`, compared with the #2843 head `eae027d55`). Each test has its own cause. They have one root: the solidcore mesh has more and different outline vertices, and three planners choose a start or an order from those vertices.

**1. The loop that crosses itself (keep_law corner check)**
- The region of the pocket is good: 3 loops (the stock, the part hole, the Ø25 bore). `connected_pieces(region)` passes.
- The error comes from `connected_pieces(&leftover)` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs`. `leftover` is the bore piece less its own swept area (`center.offset(reach)`). That gives a thin cusp at each chord vertex of the bore.
- One cusp is a bow-tie of 11 points: X 9.518..9.753, Y -8.096..-7.815, radius 12.496..12.500, area 1.2e-4 mm². Segment 2-3 crosses segment 10-0. The width is a few microns.
- `Region::new` refuses a loop that crosses itself. The area is just above `PIECE_AREA_MIN` (1e-4), so the loop is not skipped first.
- On `eae027d55` the bore has fewer chords and no cusp crosses itself. The check runs and names 7 corners.
- A local fix is possible: read each output loop of a boolean with `Region::from_slices` (the even-odd reading) in `connected_pieces`. A loop that does not cross itself gives the same result. This fix does not change the tests 1-3 below.

**Test 1** (`the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`, the assert at line 251)
- The pass start moves from (-31.789, 8.842) to (-31.878, 8.513).
- On `eae027d55` the note is "the horizontal arc fits only under its radius - flown at 1.500 mm". On the branch the note is "the horizontal arc entry does not fit".
- The four "pass start ... is in material ... ramp along the pass instead" notes are also on `eae027d55`. The test accepts them.

**Test 2** (`an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19`)
- The notes "oblique vertical arc posted as chords" and "the ring at ... ends at its floor Z 0.000 ... levels below skipped" are on `eae027d55` too. They are not new.
- The cause is `axis_reseat` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/lead_ext.rs`. It keeps the start when the first edge of the ring is within `tol_deg` (1 degree) of an axis.
- On the branch the first edge of the outer ring is a 0.973 mm chord of the r 35 arc, from (1.054, -34.984) to (0.081, -34.999). It is 0.93 degrees off X, so no reseat occurs.
- The arc entry on a chord that is not exactly on X has no standard plane, so it is posted as chords (the note says so). That gives 0 vertical arcs.
- On `eae027d55` the first edge was out of the tolerance. The ring was reseated to the straight edge at Y 34.719, and the path got 6 G18/G19 arcs.
- This is a gap in `axis_reseat`: an edge within the tolerance is not exact enough for G18/G19. The finer chords of the r 30 arc show the gap.

**Test 3** (`fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`)
- On both heads the HSM plan is refused and "Offset rings cut this pocket instead" (the same note).
- Branch / `eae027d55`:
  - feed moves: 1721 / 1807
  - feed length: 9098.7 / 9128.7 mm
  - feed ends at the face (distance 4.000 ± 0.05): 135 / 134
  - smallest distance to the outline: 4.0000 / 4.0000
- Only the ring order changes. On the branch the last feed is on the outer ring at the stock boundary (47.43, -39.0). On `eae027d55` it is on the face ring.
- The path reaches the face, and no material is left that `eae027d55` cuts. The operation is not incomplete. The note on the Offset-ring fallback is on both heads.

**The cylinder walls are not staggered.** The r 30 wall of `Milling-test.step` has the same 185 angles at each of its 10 Z rows. The outline has more points (fig8: 4082 / 1722 / 1095 on the branch, 3314 / 1683 / 1031 on `eae027d55`).

No toolpath gives silent wrong output. A fix for tests 1-3 changes planner behaviour (start choice, ring order, reseat tolerance) that other pins and goldens read. It is not a small local outline fix.

claimed: Codex (m3) · 2026-11-20 03:22 UTC · branch mkinney:issue/2849-corner-cusp-loop · plan: pin the loop that crosses itself in `connected_pieces(&leftover)` with a synthetic fine-chord bore on `main`, then read each boolean output loop with the even-odd rule. Tests 2 and 3 need PR B and are not in this work.

Update from the #917 worker. The three moved pins have three causes. PR B (`issue/917-solidcore-step`, stacked on #2843) fixes cause 1. Causes 2 and 3 stay open on this issue, and item 4 is a separate gap.

**1. Corner check "did not run" (fixed in PR B, commit bc5daa32d).**
- Cause: `connected_pieces` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` read each outer loop of the leftover with `Region::new`. `Region::new` refuses a loop that crosses itself. The bore leftover kept an 11-point bow-tie cusp (area 1.2e-4 mm2, 0.3 mm long).
- Fix: the loop is boolean output, not sketch input. The new helper `outer_fills` reads it with `Region::from_slices` (the even-odd reading). A simple loop gives the same single path both ways.
- The four `unreached::law` tests and `narrow_band.rs` do not change and pass. They prove that a loop which `Region::new` accepts gives the same pieces as before.
- Reading: the check names the same 7 corners as on eae027d55 (four stock corners 3 x 3, three wall boxes). The wall box edges move by 0.095 mm or less (for example X 28.995 to 35.000 on the branch, X 29.090 to 35.000 on eae027d55).
- Pins:
  - `unreached::law::a_micron_bow_tie_cusp_gives_its_lobes_and_no_error` (a hand-made bow-tie, 0.4 mm long and 2 microns high).
  - `lead_approach::the_users_pocket_names_its_seven_sharp_corners_and_the_corner_check_runs`. It fails without the fix, at the "did not run" assert.

**2. Horizontal arc entry (stays, test 1 keeps its marker).** The pass start moves from (-31.789, 8.842) to (-31.878, 8.513). The note "fits only under its radius - flown at 1.500 mm" becomes "does not fit". Test 1 still fails on that note assert (line 251) after the fix.

**3. Ring order of the fig8 EM-0800 adaptive (stays, test 3 keeps its marker and its assert).** On both heads the HSM plan is refused, and the Offset rings cut the area. The order changed by the chain law of `waterline_passes`. It is not a tie in a sort.
- `waterline_passes` lists the loops by offset (descending) and then by area. At k 0..2 the stock ring areas (20578, 21300, 22030) and the face ring areas (13824, 13169, 12523) are not equal.
- A chain takes the first listed loop whose chord from the current entry point clears.
- On the new mesh the face ring's start vertex moved. The chord from the k 2 stock ring entry (47.388, -36.657) to the k 2 face ring entry (-0.070, -36.343) now clears.
- Branch chains, end of the list: `[37, 41, 45, 49, 52, 53, 55, 57]` and then `[54, 56]`. Thus the k 1 and k 0 stock rings are cut last, and the last feed ends on the stock ring.
- I did not take the chain reading on eae027d55.
- Test 3 removes no less material: 9098.7 mm of feed on the branch and 9128.7 mm on eae027d55. The smallest distance to the part is 4.0000 on both.

**4. `axis_reseat` (separate item, stays).** This is the cause of test 2.
- The first edge of the ring is a 0.973 mm chord from (1.054451, -34.983548) to (0.081123, -34.999342). It is 0.93 degrees off X, which is inside the 1 degree tolerance, so `axis_reseat` keeps the start.
- Then no standard plane fits: 0 G18/G19 arcs on the branch, 6 on eae027d55.
- The gap is on main too, for each start edge between 0 and 1 degree off an axis.

Each fallback has a note. None of them gives silent wrong output.

fix on issue/2849-corner-cusp-loop · PR #2850 · pinned by `machining2d::unreached::law::a_chord_cusp_that_crosses_itself_does_not_stop_the_corner_check` · merges when reviewed

PR #2850 is partial. It ends with `Refs #2849`, so the merge does not close this issue.

- It fixes the corner check: `connected_pieces` reads each boolean output loop with `Region::from_slices`.
- The defect is on `main` without the solidcore mesh. A synthetic 25 mm bore with 50 chords and a 4 mm tool shows it.
- It does not change tests 1 to 3. Their causes are the pass start choice, `axis_reseat` and the ring order, as the diagnosis above says.
- Tests 1 to 3 and their `known-fail #2849` markers need PR B of #917. They stay open work on this issue.

claimed: Codex (m3) · 2026-11-21 17:48 UTC · branch mkinney:issue/2849-three-pins · plan: PR B (#2904) is merged. Fix the three `known-fail #2849` pins (axis_reseat tolerance, arc entry start, ring order) on main and remove the markers.

Codex (m3) stops on this issue. The quick gate failed two times for real reasons. The claim is released. Held work is on `mkinney:issue/2849-three-pins` at `bfc1dc03b`.

**Test 2 (`an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19`): fixed on the branch.**
- Cause: `axis_reseat` kept the start for each first edge within `axis_tol`. `entry_arc::true_arc` posts G18/G19 only for an exact axis edge.
- Fix: keep the start only when the first edge is exactly on an axis, or when no edge is nearer an axis.
- Pins: the app test passes. New unit tests are in `lead_ext::reseat_tests`. The old `lead_ext.rs` makes the app test red.

**Test 1 (`the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`): fixed on the branch.**
- Cause: the first pass starts on a ring. The arc tangent comes from the fitted walk arc. The ring polyline that returns to the start is 0.6 micron outside that tangent line. The hull of the arc crosses the ring behind the start, on both sides and at each radius.
- Fix: `descent_xy::plan_xy` tries the old tangent first. If no radius fits, it tries the direction of the closing edge of the first ring. It uses that direction only within 1e-3 rad of the old tangent.
- Pins: the app test passes, and `xy_arc_entry` passes (5 tests). The old `descent_xy.rs` makes the app test red.

**Test 3 (`fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`): not fixed. It keeps its marker.**
- I tried this change in `waterline_passes`: try the step to the other ring family at the same offset last. Test 3 then passed, because the part face was cut last.
- Then `corner_arc_radius::the_crossing_law_keeps_the_arc_turns_and_crosses_nowhere` failed (OffsetRings, r 1 mm). One corner stayed sharp with "an arc there would cross another feed".
- The reason: the chain ends with a 1.66 mm diagonal chord into the sharp corner of the outer wall ring.
- The two pins want opposite wall orders on a holed area. The ring planner does not know which wall is the finished wall. The maintainer must decide the law. One option: the outside containment names the part face as the last wall.

**Gate failures:**
1. `corner_arc_radius` (the ring order change). I removed that change.
2. `xy_arc_entry::the_arc_entry_starts_each_level_with_a_g17_arc_tangent_to_its_first_pass`. The first test-1 fix always used the closing edge, and it broke tangency on a polygon circle. The fallback on the branch fixes it. The full quick gate was not run again on `bfc1dc03b`.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/2849-three-pins.md` on the branch.
